name: Vajrasana (Thunderbolt Pose)
target_benefit: Improves digestion, prevents acidity, and strengthens pelvic muscles.
steps: Kneel on the floor with your knees and toes touching.
Sit back on your heels.
Keep your head, neck, and spine completely straight.
Place your palms on your thighs facing downwards.
Close your eyes and breathe deeply and steadily.

name: Sheetali Pranayama (Cooling Breath)
target_benefit: Cools the body, reduces acidity, and calms the nervous system.
steps: Sit in a comfortable cross-legged position with your spine straight.
Stick your tongue out slightly and roll the edges inward to form a tube.
Inhale deeply and slowly through the tubular tongue.
Close your mouth and hold your breath for a few seconds.
Exhale slowly through your nose.

name: Malasana (Garland Pose)
target_benefit: Stimulates metabolism, relieves constipation, and opens the hips.
steps: Stand with your feet slightly wider than hip-width apart.
Bend your knees and lower your hips into a deep squat.
Bring your palms together at your chest in a prayer position.
Press your elbows gently against the inside of your knees to open your hips.
Keep your spine straight and hold the pose while breathing deeply.

name: Pawanmuktasana (Wind-Relieving Pose)
target_benefit: Releases abdominal gas, improves digestion, and relieves lower back pain.
steps: Lie flat on your back with your legs straight and arms by your side.
Inhale deeply, then exhale and bring your knees to your chest.
Clasp your hands around your shins to hug your knees close.
Lift your head and try to touch your chin or forehead to your knees.
Hold the pose, then exhale and release your legs back to the floor.

name: Shavasana (Corpse Pose)
target_benefit: Deeply relaxes the body, reduces stress, and lowers blood pressure.
steps: Lie flat on your back completely relaxed.
Keep your legs comfortably apart with your toes falling outward.
Rest your arms slightly away from your body with your palms facing up.
Close your eyes and let your breathing become natural and rhythmic.
Consciously relax every part of your body from your toes to your head.

name: Ardha Matsyendrasana (Half Lord of the Fishes Pose)
target_benefit: Massages abdominal organs, detoxifies the liver, and improves spinal mobility.
steps: Sit with your legs stretched out in front of you.
Bend your left knee and tuck your left heel under your right hip.
Cross your right leg over your left knee and plant your right foot flat.
Twist your torso to the right, hooking your left elbow outside your right knee.
Place your right hand behind you for support and gaze over your right shoulder.

name: Surya Namaskar (Sun Salutation)
target_benefit: Full body cardiovascular workout, improves flexibility, and boosts immunity.
steps: Stand tall with palms together at your chest (Pranamasana).
Inhale, stretch your arms up and arch your back (Hastottanasana).
Exhale, bend forward and touch the floor beside your feet (Padahastasana).
Inhale, step your right leg back, drop the knee, and look up (Ashwa Sanchalanasana).
Retain breath, step the left leg back into a plank position (Dandasana).
Exhale, lower your knees, chest, and chin to the floor (Ashtanga Namaskara).
Inhale, slide forward and lift your chest into Cobra pose (Bhujangasana).
Exhale, lift your hips up into Downward Dog (Adho Mukha Svanasana).
Repeat the lunges with the opposite legs to return to a standing position.

name: Paschimottanasana (Seated Forward Bend)
target_benefit: Calms the mind, stimulates the liver and kidneys, and relieves stress.
steps: Sit with your legs stretched out straight in front of you.
Inhale deeply and raise both arms above your head.
Exhale and lean forward from your hips, keeping your spine straight.
Reach for your toes, ankles, or shins, depending on your flexibility.
Drop your head toward your knees and hold the stretch.

name: Kapalabhati Pranayama (Skull Shining Breath)
target_benefit: Clears the respiratory tract, boosts metabolism, and improves brain function.
steps: Sit comfortably with your spine erect and hands resting on your knees.
Take a deep breath in through your nose.
Exhale forcefully through your nose while pulling your navel in toward your spine.
Allow the inhalation to happen passively and naturally without effort.
Repeat this rhythmic, forceful exhalation for 30 to 60 seconds.

name: Baddha Konasana (Butterfly Pose)
target_benefit: Stimulates reproductive organs, relieves menstrual discomfort, and opens hips.
steps: Sit on the floor with your legs stretched straight out.
Bend your knees and bring the soles of your feet together.
Pull your heels as close to your pelvis as comfortable.
Clasp your feet tightly with your hands.
Keep your back straight and gently flap your knees up and down like butterfly wings.

name: Viparita Karani (Legs-Up-The-Wall Pose)
target_benefit: Improves blood circulation, reduces edema, and relieves tired legs.
steps: Sit on the floor next to a wall, with your side touching the wall.
Lie back onto the floor and swing your legs up onto the wall.
Scoot your hips as close to the wall as possible.
Rest your arms by your sides with your palms facing up.
Close your eyes, breathe deeply, and remain here for 5 to 15 minutes.

name: Balasana (Child's Pose)
target_benefit: Releases tension in the back and shoulders, and relieves fatigue and anxiety.
steps: Kneel on the floor with your toes together and knees slightly apart.
Exhale and lower your torso down between your knees.
Stretch your arms out in front of you or rest them alongside your body.
Rest your forehead gently on the floor.
Breathe deeply and let your entire body relax.

name: Nadi Shodhana Pranayama (Alternate Nostril Breathing)
target_benefit: Balances the left and right hemispheres of the brain, reduces anxiety.
steps: Sit comfortably with a straight spine and relax your shoulders.
Use your right thumb to close your right nostril and inhale deeply through the left.
Close the left nostril with your ring finger, release the thumb, and exhale through the right.
Inhale through the right nostril, close it, and exhale through the left.
This completes one cycle. Repeat for 5-10 minutes.

name: Dhanurasana (Bow Pose)
target_benefit: Expands the chest, stimulates abdominal organs, and improves posture.
steps: Lie flat on your stomach with your feet hip-width apart and arms by your side.
Bend your knees and reach your hands backward to grasp your ankles.
Inhale deeply and lift your chest and thighs off the floor.
Look straight ahead and balance your body weight on your abdomen.
Hold the pose, then exhale and gently release.

name: Bhujangasana (Cobra Pose)
target_benefit: Strengthens the spine, opens the heart and lungs, and relieves asthma.
steps: Lie on your stomach with your legs straight and feet together.
Place your palms flat on the floor directly under your shoulders.
Keep your elbows tucked in close to your body.
Inhale and slowly lift your head, chest, and abdomen off the floor.
Keep your navel on the floor and look upwards.

name: Matsyasana (Fish Pose)
target_benefit: Stretches the neck and chest, highly beneficial for respiratory issues.
steps: Lie flat on your back with your legs straight and feet together.
Place your hands under your hips, palms facing down.
Press your forearms and elbows into the floor and lift your chest upward.
Tilt your head back and lightly rest the crown of your head on the floor.
Breathe deeply into your expanded chest.

name: Ujjayi Pranayama (Ocean Breath)
target_benefit: Soothes the nervous system, warms the body, and regulates blood pressure.
steps: Sit in a comfortable cross-legged posture with your spine erect.
Take a long, deep breath in through your nose.
Slightly constrict the back of your throat as you inhale and exhale.
This constriction should create a soft, hissing sound, similar to ocean waves.
Keep your mouth closed and continue breathing smoothly and rhythmically.

name: Jal Neti (Nasal Cleansing Kriya)
target_benefit: Clears nasal passages, relieves sinusitis, and improves breathing.
steps: Prepare a Neti pot with lukewarm, sterile water and a pinch of non-iodized salt.
Stand over a sink and tilt your head slightly to one side.
Insert the spout of the Neti pot gently into the upper nostril.
Breathe through your mouth while pouring the water, allowing it to flow out the lower nostril.
Blow your nose gently and repeat on the other side.

name: Gomukhasana (Cow Face Pose)
target_benefit: Stretches shoulders and arms, relieves frozen shoulder and neck tension.
steps: Sit on the floor and cross your right leg over your left, stacking your knees.
Raise your right arm toward the ceiling, bend your elbow, and drop your hand down your back.
Reach your left arm behind your back, bend the elbow, and reach up to clasp your right hand.
Keep your spine straight and your chest open.
Hold for a few breaths, release, and repeat on the opposite side.

name: Anulom Vilom Pranayama
target_benefit: Clears blockages in energy channels, supports respiratory and mental health.
steps: Sit in a comfortable posture and close your eyes.
Use your right thumb to close your right nostril.
Inhale deeply through your left nostril.
Close your left nostril with your ring finger, release the right nostril, and exhale.
Inhale through the right nostril, close it, and exhale through the left.

name: Adho Mukha Svanasana (Downward-Facing Dog)
target_benefit: Energizes the body, stretches hamstrings, and relieves headache.
steps: Start on your hands and knees in a tabletop position.
Spread your fingers wide and press your palms flat into the mat.
Tuck your toes under, exhale, and lift your hips up and back.
Straighten your legs as much as possible and press your heels toward the floor.
Let your head hang loosely between your arms, forming an inverted 'V' shape.

name: Bhastrika Pranayama (Bellows Breath)
target_benefit: Generates internal heat, clears the lungs, and boosts immunity.
steps: Sit cross-legged with your spine straight and shoulders relaxed.
Take a deep breath in, fully expanding your lungs.
Exhale forcefully and quickly through your nose.
Immediately inhale forcefully and quickly.
Continue this rapid, powerful breathing for a few rounds, using your diaphragm like a bellows.

name: Simhasana (Lion Pose)
target_benefit: Relieves tension in the face and chest, excellent for sore throat and speech defects.
steps: Kneel down and cross your ankles behind you, sitting back on your heels.
Place your palms on your knees with your fingers spread wide.
Inhale deeply through your nose.
Open your mouth wide, stick your tongue out as far as possible toward your chin.
Exhale forcefully with a 'ha' sound while looking up toward your eyebrows.

name: Setu Bandhasana (Bridge Pose)
target_benefit: Strengthens the back, glutes, and hamstrings; opens the chest.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Place your arms alongside your body with your palms facing down.
Inhale, press your feet into the floor, and slowly lift your hips upward.
Roll your shoulders under your body and interlace your fingers behind your back if possible.
Hold the pose, breathing deeply, then slowly roll your spine back down to the mat.

name: Vrikshasana (Tree Pose)
target_benefit: Improves balance, focus, and concentration; strengthens the legs.
steps: Stand tall with your feet together and arms by your sides.
Shift your weight onto your left leg.
Bend your right knee and place the sole of your right foot on your inner left thigh (avoid the knee joint).
Once balanced, bring your hands together in front of your chest in a prayer position.
Hold your gaze on a fixed point in front of you to maintain balance.

name: Yoga Nidra (Yogic Sleep)
target_benefit: Deep guided relaxation that reduces insomnia, stress, and anxiety.
steps: Lie flat on your back in Shavasana (Corpse Pose) in a quiet room.
Close your eyes and take several deep, calming breaths.
Listen to an audio guide or mentally scan your body from your toes up to your head.
Consciously command each body part to relax as you focus your awareness on it.
Remain completely still and deeply relaxed, staying awake but in a state of deep rest.

name: Trataka (Candle Gazing)
target_benefit: Improves vision, relieves eye strain, and enhances memory.
steps: Sit comfortably in a dark room with your spine straight.
Place a lit candle at eye level, about two to three feet away.
Gaze steadily at the flame without blinking.
Continue staring until your eyes begin to water slightly.
Close your eyes gently and visualize the flame between your eyebrows.

name: Ustrasana (Camel Pose)
target_benefit: Stretches the entire front of the body, improves posture, and relieves fatigue.
steps: Kneel on the floor with your knees hip-width apart.
Place your hands on your lower back for support, fingers pointing down.
Inhale, engage your core, and gently lean back, pushing your hips forward.
If comfortable, reach your hands back one at a time to grasp your heels.
Let your head gently drop back and hold the stretch.

name: Tadasana (Mountain Pose)
target_benefit: Improves posture, strengthens thighs, and relieves sciatica.
steps: Stand with your feet together or slightly apart, arms resting by your sides.
Distribute your body weight evenly across both feet.
Engage your thigh muscles and tuck your tailbone slightly.
Roll your shoulders back and down, keeping your neck long and straight.
Breathe deeply and hold the posture steadily.

name: Trikonasana (Triangle Pose)
target_benefit: Stretches legs and torso, mobilizes hips, and relieves backache.
steps: Stand with your feet wide apart (about 3 to 4 feet).
Turn your right foot out 90 degrees and your left foot slightly inward.
Raise your arms out to the sides, parallel to the floor.
Exhale and hinge at your right hip, reaching your right hand down to your shin, ankle, or the floor.
Extend your left arm straight up toward the ceiling and gaze up at your left hand.

name: Marjaryasana-Bitilasana (Cat-Cow Pose)
target_benefit: Improves spinal flexibility and relieves tension in the neck and back.
steps: Start on your hands and knees in a tabletop position.
Inhale, drop your belly toward the floor, and lift your chin and chest to look up (Cow Pose).
Exhale, draw your belly button toward your spine, round your back, and tuck your chin (Cat Pose).
Continue flowing smoothly between these two poses, matching the movement to your breath.
Repeat for 5-10 cycles.

name: Sarvangasana (Shoulder Stand)
target_benefit: Stimulates the thyroid gland, improves circulation, and prevents hair fall.
steps: Lie flat on your back with your arms by your sides.
Inhale and lift both legs up to a 90-degree angle.
Press your hands into the floor and lift your hips and lower back off the ground.
Support your back with your hands and straighten your legs upward toward the ceiling.
Rest your weight on your shoulders and upper arms, never on your neck.

name: Bhramari Pranayama (Bee Breath)
target_benefit: Instantly calms the mind, relieves tension headaches, and reduces anger.
steps: Sit in a comfortable position with your spine straight and eyes closed.
Place your index fingers gently over your ear cartilage to block out external sound.
Take a deep breath in through your nose.
Exhale slowly while making a continuous, smooth humming sound like a bee.
Focus on the vibration created in your head.

name: Navasana (Boat Pose)
target_benefit: Strengthens the core, improves digestion, and supports weight management.
steps: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat.
Lean back slightly, keeping your spine straight and chest lifted.
Lift your feet off the floor until your shins are parallel to the ground.
If comfortable, straighten your legs to form a 'V' shape with your body.
Extend your arms straight out in front of you, parallel to the floor.

name: Halasana (Plow Pose)
target_benefit: Calms the brain, stimulates the thyroid, and stretches the spine and shoulders.
steps: Begin in Sarvangasana (Shoulder Stand) with your legs extended upward.
Exhale and slowly lower your legs over your head.
Try to touch your toes to the floor behind your head, keeping your legs straight.
Release your hands from your back and place them flat on the floor.
Hold the pose, then gently roll your spine back down to the mat.

name: Agnisar Kriya
target_benefit: Stimulates the digestive fire, tones abdominal organs, and improves sluggish metabolism.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and bend your knees slightly.
Lean forward and place your hands firmly on your thighs.
Exhale completely, emptying your lungs of all air.
While holding your breath out, rapidly flap your abdomen in and out.
Stop the movement, inhale deeply, and rest before repeating.

name: Griva Sanchalana (Neck Rolls)
target_benefit: Releases accumulated tension in the cervical spine and shoulders.
steps: Sit or stand comfortably with your spine straight and shoulders relaxed.
Slowly drop your chin toward your chest.
Inhale and gently roll your right ear toward your right shoulder.
Exhale and roll your chin back down to your chest.
Inhale and roll your left ear toward your left shoulder, continuing the gentle semicircles.

name: Palming
target_benefit: Soothes the optic nerve, relaxes facial muscles, and relieves eye strain.
steps: Sit comfortably and close your eyes.
Rub the palms of your hands together vigorously until they feel warm.
Gently cup your warm palms over your closed eyes without pressing on the eyeballs.
Ensure no light enters between your fingers.
Breathe deeply and let the warmth relax your eye muscles for 1 to 2 minutes.
